text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - British shares fell, dragged down by lower bonds, a weaker performance on Wall Street and a call for higher interest rates from the Bank of England's deputy governor. The FTSE 100 index fell 27.7 points to 4,078.8, with decliners ahead of gainers by a 7-2 margin.

FRANKFURT - Shares edged higher and dealers said there was disappointment that Wall Street's overnight close failed to add much to last week's strong rally. The DAX-30 index added 4.81 points to 2,886.13.
PARIS - Prices retreated in line with Wall Street but remained above the 2,300 level. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 4.98 points at 2,301.69.
ZURICH - Shares closed little changed in fairly active trading. The broad SPI rose 4.58 points to 2,510.80.

TOKYO - Stocks fell to their lowest close in 13 months despite the yen's recovery and Wall Street's rally overnight, beset by lingering worries over the economy. The benchmark Nikkei 225 average fell 549.81 points or 2.83 percent to 18,896.19, the lowest close since Dec. 5, 1995.
HONG KONG - Stocks gave back early gains to end weak on concern about higher interest rates. The Hang Seng index closed 23.77 points lower at 13,420.16.
SYDNEY - Stocks fell as sentiment softened and the gold sector tumbled in response to falling bullion prices. The All Ordinaries index lost 9.1 points to 2,400.7.

JOHANNESBURG - A jump in futures contracts propelled industrial shares higher. The industrial index surged 61.7 points to 7,944.2. The all-share index climbed 37.9 points to 6,614.1 but the gold index fell 9.9 points to 1,412.3.
